item.description: Israeli forces demolish illegal construction near the security fence and an ancient archaeological site in two-day enforcement operation in Area C.

item.description: After making Aliyah from France, cousins Gad and Elior enlist in the IDF’s Hasmonean Brigade, driven by faith, duty and a desire to defend Israel.

item.title: Netanyahu hails security agreement with Greece
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated: "The security agreement signed today with Greece, one of the largest in the country's history, is a direct continuation of the Eastern Mediterranean alliance we forged a decade ago with Greece and Cyprus. It serves as further proof of the tremendous capabilities of Israel's defense and technological industries. This move expresses Israel's strength, the confidence in our defense exports, and the strengthening of regional alliances."

item.title: Preventing nuclear war is an urgent obligation
item.description: A nuclear war - any nuclear war - would resemble an incurable disease. Of necessity, all meaningful “therapies" must lie in prevention. Opinion.

item.description: Police have decided to increase security around Supreme Court Justice and Central Elections Committee Chairman Noam Sohlberg following a situation assessment and intelligence that was received.

item.title: Draft crackdown could bring thousands of Breslov Hassidim to Meron
item.description: With draft dodgers facing obstacles to leaving Israel, Breslov organizers prepare Meron for thousands who may be unable to spend Rosh Hashanah in Uman.

item.title: Desalination plants shut down for hours due to weather conditions
item.description: Unusual weather conditions caused severe turbidity in the seawater, leading to the shutdown of desalination plants south of Hadera.

item.description: Iran responds to Trump's threats: 'We will respond harshly to any attack'

item.title: After Rabbi Yosef’s attack, Rabbi Kook’s glowing words for Rabbi Lior resurface
item.description: Following Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef’s criticism of Rabbi Dov Lior, a historic letter resurfaces revealing Rabbi Tzvi Yehuda Kook’s glowing praise for him.

item.title: Trump on Iran: 'We're going to hit them hard'
item.description:
US President Donald Trump told Fox News on Monday that the US will respond to the Iranian attack on US forces overnight in Jordan. "We're going to hit them hard; there will be a response."
The President indicated that all except for one missile were intercepted.

item.title: Trump: 'Iran is Dead'
item.description: US President calls Iran a 'failed state' that has killed over 100,00 of its own people.

item.title: 18 million shekels: Force 100 soldiers sue prosecutors, police and Channel 12
item.description: Three Force 100 soldiers seek 18 million shekels from prosecutors, law enforcement officials and media figures, alleging false arrest, leaks and defamation.

item.title: Repairing a world that hates us
item.description: As catastrophe strikes Nepal, Israelis have once again travelled thousands of miles to help strangers. Real Tikkun Olam demands that we perfect the world God rules - and what better way than to try repair a broken world, even when parts of that world despise us.

item.title: Pharmacists suspected of stealing medications from IDF base
item.description: Two veteran pharmacists were arrested on suspicion of taking tens of thousands of medications intended for soldiers and selling them on the black market for tens of thousands of shekels.

item.title: Leket Israel Founder and Chairman: 700,000 meals needed for Rosh Hashanah
item.description: Leket Israel Founder and Chairman Joseph Gitler discusses rescuing surplus food, supporting Israeli farmers and expanding food assistance ahead of Rosh Hashanah, with a goal of distributing more than 700,000 meals to people in need.

item.title: Mother of missing 10-year-old: ‘He used my son to beg for money’
item.description: Shiran, mother of 10-year-old Yaheli, reveals how a 20-year-old allegedly manipulated her son, took him on a bus to Bnei Brak and used him to collect donations.

item.title: Making the Jewish World like haredim again
item.description: After years in which Israel’s haredi political representatives made too many Jews resent us, Moti Leitner and his new party may be achieving what once seemed impossible. Opinion.

item.title: Six days after Nepal flood disaster: Another Israeli reported missing
item.description: Katrina (Katya) Sakovich disappeared after a flash flood struck the area of the Rasuwagadhi-Gyirong border crossing. Her sister is due to travel to Nepal and join the search efforts. Another Israeli, a man in his 60s, is still missing.

item.title: Foreign Ministry confirms: Another Israeli missing in Nepal
item.description:
The Foreign Ministry has confirmed that Israeli citizen Katrina Sakovich has been missing since the flood disaster in Nepal.
In addition, searches are continuing for another Israeli citizen, a man in his 60s.

item.title: Yesh Atid shakeup: Meir Cohen bows out of Knesset race
item.description: Lapid’s longtime political partner gives up his spot for the party’s 'next generation' but says he isn’t leaving Yesh Atid.

item.title: Nepal flood disaster: 590 foreign nationals still missing
item.description:
Nepal's Foreign Ministry has updated the number of foreign nationals still missing following the floods which struck the country, saying that 590 people remain unaccounted for.
The missing individuals are citizens of 39 different countries. So far, 323 foreign nationals have been rescued.

item.title: ‘Humanitarian aid’ truck caught smuggling liquid nicotine into Gaza
item.description: Inspectors uncover 100 bottles hidden inside drinks at Kerem Shalom; truck seized and Israeli company’s Gaza aid permit suspended.
